title: Streaming JSON terminator healing and graceful silence handling
creator: Ethan Moore
description: Problem: We frequently see LLM streaming responses cut off mid-JSON token or emit extra bytes when downstream connections are interrupted or when autoscaling preempts workers. Current heuristics (closing on the last '}' or ']' seen) lead to incorrect tool-call boundaries, spuriously accepted partial objects, or corrupted escapes when truncation happens mid-hex/unicode sequence. This ticket designs a pragmatic "terminator healing" strategy plus a graceful silence policy for client-facing streams to reduce data loss, enable safe retries, and preserve tool-call idempotency.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime emits streaming chunks annotated with minimal per-chunk metadata (sequence id, last-well-formed-offset) without changing public API shape. 2) Client/SDKs can detect a truncated JSON fragment and attempt a conservative heal that either recovers a single top-level object or signals a safe retry. 3) Tool/function call boundaries are never inferred from a healed fragment if function call metadata is incomplete; instead runtime will surface a concrete 'truncated-toolcall' terminal event. 4) End-to-end tests covering: mid-escape truncation, multi-object NDJSON with truncation boundary, interleaved toolcall + text streaming, and simulated connection preemption. 5) PRs with implementation and SDK adapters merged + canary on 10% traffic without increased error rate.
design_notes: Key ideas: (a) Stream chunk introspection: augment internal stream envelopes with a compact 'safe_offset' integer indicating byte offset up to which payload is syntactically valid UTF-8 and JSON-parseable for complete top-level entities. This is internal only and surfaced to SDKs as a boolean 'has_partial' with a checksum on last complete object. (b) Terminator healing rules: prefer to close the smallest number of open delimiters; when encountering an incomplete escape (e.g., '\u' plus <incomplete hex>), supply a best-effort replacement (U+FFFD) only for diagnostics and not as part of any tool-call payload used for side effects. (c) Tool-call contract: tool-call must be emitted as a separate framed sub-event; partial tool-call frames will cause the runtime to emit a 'truncated-toolcall' event with a stable id so callers can decide retry semantics. (d) Backpressure & silence: when the server detects a worker preemption or long GC it should emit a 'graceful-silence' sentinel chunk allowing clients to wait with exponential jitter before retrying rather than aborting immediately. (e) Compatibility shim: SDK adapters for python/js will expose a 'recover_fragment' helper that prefers non-destructive signalling over silent mutation and returns structured diagnostics to the application.
implementation_plan: 1) Add stream envelope fields to internal transport (fast-path only, preserved under feature flag) -> small runtime change. 2) Implement terminator healing algorithm in streaming decoder library (C++/Rust) and export conservative API. 3) Wire 'truncated-toolcall' event path and record telemetry counters. 4) SDK changes (py/js) to detect 'graceful-silence' and provide recover_fragment helper and user-visible error classes. 5) Integration tests in CI simulating partial payloads and preemption. 6) Canary rollout and metrics dashboard. Rollback plan: disable feature flag and revert SDK adapters if errors spike.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Healing may mask subtle semantic errors or cause clients to believe a tool was invoked when it wasn't. Mitigation: never auto-apply healed content to stateful side-effectful tool calls; always require explicit 'confirm' from caller after a healed fragment. Risk: Adding envelope fields increases RPC size. Mitigation: keep fields compact and enable under opt-in flag for 90 days before default-on. Risk: Clients with older SDKs may ignore new sentinel events. Mitigation: runtime will also log deprecation notices and provide fallbacks (close stream with code 410 + explanation).
test_plan: - Unit tests for decoder on artificially truncated byte streams (UTF-8 split inside multi-byte char, '\u' broken sequences, partial multibyte codepoints). - Property tests generating random JSON with streaming boundaries. - End-to-end test harness that simulates preemption: start stream, kill worker mid-response, verify runtime emits 'graceful-silence' and 'truncated-toolcall' as specified. - SDK integration tests that exercise recover_fragment and verify no side-effectful tool call executed without explicit confirm. - Perf regression tests: <5% latency p95 increase on streaming-critical paths.
